title: Reality Monitoring Criteria Applied to LLM Chain-of-Thought Deception Detection
original_idea: Collect CoT traces from a reasoning model under honest and deceptive conditions. Apply Reality Monitoring coding criteria (detail richness, internal consistency, meta-cognitive markers). Train a logistic regression classifier. Test generalization across model families.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Offers a lightweight, model-agnostic screening tool for deception. Impact pathway is clear but depends on whether Reality Monitoring criteria actually transfer to LLM outputs, which is uncertain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Collecting CoT traces is straightforward. Hand-coding Reality Monitoring criteria requires understanding the psychology framework. Training logistic regression is basic. Cross-model generalization testing adds scope. Feasible but requires careful operationalization of the coding criteria.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Moderately scoped. The core experiment (code traces, train classifier) is clear, but cross-model generalization testing and operationalizing Reality Monitoring criteria for LLM outputs adds breadth. Could be narrowed to a single model family.

novelty.reasoning: CoT monitoring for deception is active (OpenAI 2025, LIARS' BENCH benchmark). DeceptionBench provides 150 scenarios across 5 domains. LLM-based deception detection using emotion features and classifiers is established (LieXBerta, RoBERTa-based approaches). However, the specific application of Reality Monitoring criteria (detail richness, internal consistency, meta-cognitive markers) from forensic psychology to LLM chain-of-thought traces is novel. Existing CoT monitoring uses general-purpose LLM monitors or probe classifiers, not structured forensic psychology coding frameworks. The logistic regression classifier trained on RM-coded features from CoT traces is a distinct and unexplored approach.
